### Book X. The Ten-Stringed Lyre of Nature.

<margin>How we are united to GOD through the degrees of the Angelic orders.</margin>
...harmony and the strengthening of all virtues; and since the Trinity communicates itself in a threefold manner, it willed to govern man and all things produced for his sake through a threefold degree. In the **Principalities** <note>The seventh of the nine traditional angelic orders, believed to watch over nations and provinces.</note>, God established the governance of Empires, Kingdoms, and Provinces. In the **Archangels**, He placed the care of Kings and Princes themselves. In the **Angels**, He decreed the care of individual human beings. Thus it came to pass that, just as God flows down into us from His fruitful Monad <note>original: "monade." The "One" or the indivisible source of all being in Neoplatonic philosophy.</note> through the tripartite order of Angels, so we might ascend through them back to GOD as if by a **Jacob’s Ladder**. 

For it is certain, as **Dionysius** <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a 5th-century theologian whose "Celestial Hierarchy" defined the nine orders of angels.</note> testifies, that we can be purged, illuminated, and perfected not only by the lower intelligences, but also by the higher ones. Through the diligent practice of all virtues, we may become companions of these Hierarchical minds, according to the specific degree of virtue that flourishes most within us. This occurs if we rightly tune our mind’s **decachordon** <note>original: "decachordon." A ten-stringed lyre; here a metaphor for the human soul.</note> to the angelic ten-stringed lyre. If we stretch the string of virtue corresponding to a specific hierarchical string until it resonates perfectly, we become conformed to the minds of that order and will harmoniously obtain from GOD the virtues proper to that rank. 

<margin>The greatest secret in the Kabbalah.</margin>
This is the greatest secret of all in the **Kabbalah**; the Masters of secret Theology report that by this means alone have the Holy Men of GOD existed as performers of miraculous works. <margin>How we may be made like the Angels.</margin> For if we strive to conform ourselves to any order through the study of similar virtues—once we are purged from dissonances by the harmony of the whole—we shall easily ascend into that rank. Hence, some Holy Men of GOD, through the heat of divine love, have turned into **Seraphim** <note>The highest order of angels, associated with burning love.</note>; others, through the divine study of contemplation, have become **Cherubim**. There have even been those who, by perpetually suffering divine things <note>A reference to "patire divina," a mystical state of passive reception of God's presence through suffering or ecstasy.</note>, were assumed into the **Thrones**. Since many angels fell from every order, it was necessary to assume others to restore them; and none were assumed except humans, according to the degree of virtue that GOD had bestowed upon them while on earth.

<margin>Why subjects naturally fear their princes.</margin>
From this, it is also clear why GOD struck fear of Princes into the hearts of peoples and subjects. Is a King not a man similar to other men? Yet we see everyone submit to him with the highest reverence and fear. This could happen by no rational means unless GOD had impressed upon him the **character of His own fear** <note>original: "characterem timoris sui." A "character" in this sense is a spiritual mark or indelible seal of authority.</note>. Once a Prince is marked and elevated by this, others are compelled by a certain reverential fear and a hidden force, which God executes entirely through the order of those supreme **Principalities**. 

<margin>The source of the ruins and transfers of kingdoms and empires.</margin>
However, if Kings and Princes, through a life made unworthy and contaminated by crimes, place an obstacle to the influence of both GOD and the Principalities, the character of the fear of GOD is immediately erased from the Prince as if by public sins. The people then turn from harmony to dissonance; rebellions are stirred up, and the Prince is cast off as one unworthy of the character of divine fear. Consequently, the mutations of empires, the transfers of kingdoms, and the uprooting of Principalities and republics have no other origin than what we have stated. Therefore, let a Prince remember to order his life and cultivate justice and piety so that he may always find the Archangels (the presiding spirits) favorable to him; for without their perpetual guardianship and assistance, neither the kingdom nor the Ruler can survive.

<margin>Why even the most ferocious beasts spontaneously submit to man.</margin>
For the same reason, GOD impressed the character of fear upon even the most ferocious animals, so that they would be subject to and obey man, for whose sake they were created. We see a boy, though weak in strength, lead a huge Elephant or a most ferocious Lion by the hand, ruling and imperiously directing them with lashes wherever he wishes; and the beast obeys him in all things, submitting itself entirely. Certainly, this is for no other reason than that the law of order so prescribes, and because the **character of the fear of GOD** impressed upon man forces all things to be subject to him. 

The same is observed in the order of animals: the reason one animal fears another, even if the other is much inferior in strength and size (as the Elephant fears the ram, or the Lion fears the rooster), is that they are under the protection of a higher order and bear a "character of principality." When lower creatures recognize this by natural instinct, they revere it. You see, therefore, how all things, joined by a wonderful bond, resonate together.

<margin>A marvelous event in the election of Pope Paul V.</margin>
This harmony shines through even in fortuitous events (if indeed anything in the nature of things can be called fortuitous or accidental). For example, in the time of Pope Paul V <note>Camillo Borghese, reigned 1605–1621.</note>, shortly before his election, an Eagle was released from its bonds and flew away to perch upon an image of a **Dragon**—the heraldic symbol of the Borghese family. This signaled the election of a Pope from that same family. GOD willed, as it occurred to some minds, that through...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of how human virtues and the natural world are structured according to the nine orders of the angelic hierarchy. The Angels of the **Principalities** <note>The seventh order of angels, said to guide nations and leaders.</note> indicate the sovereignty of the world through the omen of the princely bird <note>The eagle, often used in classical augury to represent imperial power.</note>. Because earthly sovereignty is dissonant and deformed by its very nature unless it is made harmonious within itself and with others—attaining grace and beauty through this very consonance—the ministry of those above is necessary for a Prince. <margin>What the **Virtues** influence in humans.</margin> This is achieved by the order of **Virtues** <note>The fifth order of angels, associated with strength and miracles.</note>. By their favor, once constancy and strength have been acquired, we are made powerful against the lures of vices and pleasures. 

However, so that we may also prevail against those "aerial powers" <note>Demonic forces believed in the Renaissance to inhabit the lower atmosphere.</note> full of envy and malice, the protection of the super-celestial and divine **Powers** <note>The sixth order of angels, responsible for protecting the soul against evil.</note> is necessary for us. <margin>The influence of the **Powers**.</margin> Furthermore, lest we be hindered by worldly passions, the assistance of the **Dominations** <note>The fourth order of angels, representing divine authority.</note> was necessary; <margin>The influence of the **Dominations**.</margin> by harmoniously subjecting those passions to our rational appetite, we might rule over our own selves. 

Therefore, once dominion over all lower things is obtained, it remains for us to turn toward GOD and devote ourselves to Him alone. This is accomplished if we retain the memory of super-celestial things through the aid of the **Thrones**, and contemplate those same things through **Cherubic** illumination, until at last we are united to our kin and highest parent—the divine **Monad** <note>original: "monadi." The "One" or the indivisible source of all being in Neoplatonic philosophy.</note>—through **Seraphic** ardor. 

Just as the Maker of all things descends into us with His power through these angelic degrees, so too through them let us return to Him from whom we proceeded. We move as if by certain steps of virtue, of which the first step—that of our rational nature—joins us to the **Angels** through the senses; **imagination** joins us to the **Archangels**; **fear** to the **Virtues**; **grief for sins** to the **Powers**; and **reason** to the **Principalities** (for just as these angels rule over spirits, so reason rules over the senses and passions). Furthermore, **Love** joins us to the **Dominations**; the **intellect** to the **Thrones**; the **intelligence** to the **Cherubim**; and finally, **Hope** unites us to the **Seraphim**. For these highest ones lead us most closely to GOD, who is the hope of all the ends of the earth.

<margin>Angels are the tuners of the celestial song.</margin> You see, therefore, how these ministering orders—the supreme **Harmostae** <note>original: "Harmostæ." From the Greek for "tuners" or "arrangers."</note> assisting at the divine tribunal—strive to bring all things into consonance with their Prince. Being joined with those who sing psalms, they themselves act in total concord <note>original: "ὁμονοῦντες" (homonoountes), meaning "of one mind" or "in harmony."</note> as the tuners of the celestial Song. They adapt all strings and voices upon that supreme **monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical musical intervals; here, a metaphor for the unity of God's creation.</note> of GOD to make it harmonious and most sweet. If there are any useless strings or discordant melodies, they cast them out, cut them away, and reject them, lest anything dissonant be found in the worldly, celestial, or human **polychord** <note>A multi-stringed instrument, representing the complexity of the universe.</note>. Thus, all things rejoice as the Father moves them (as **Dionysius** <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, the primary source for Renaissance angelology.</note> testifies); for being moved by GOD, they move the heavens, and they dispose our bodies and other lower things toward that consonance which the first Mover of all things commands.

# §. I I I.
## On the harmony of the celestial Ennead, which it forms with the Hierarchical Ennead.

<margin>Hierarchical music with the celestial bodies.</margin> In order that the Author and Maker of all Nature might preserve the **microcosm** <note>original: "mundum minorem." Man, viewed as a small-scale model of the entire universe.</note> (for whose sake all things were made) in the most absolute harmony, He set in motion another **Ennead** <note>A group of nine.</note>: namely, the systems of the celestial world, by whose influence the lower world is governed. These are the first **Empyrean Heaven**, the **Starry Heaven** (or firmament), and the spheres of **Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury,** and the **Moon**. 

However, since these bodies were by their own nature inanimate and incapable of motion, He attributed to each its own **Intelligences** <note>Angelic beings that act as the "souls" or "movers" of the planets.</note>. By their power, being driven by various motions, they produce various effects according to the needs of the sublunary <note>Earthly, or below the moon.</note> world; thus, the very constitution of physical nature depends on the influence of the higher bodies. These Intelligences assisting the Heavens have the care of arranging souls, while GOD—as the supreme **Choragus** <note>The leader of a choir or ancient Greek play; the "conductor" of the universe.</note>—binds the lowest things to the highest and the middle to the top into one most perfect harmony. But let the harmony of each be made more clearly manifest:

<margin>The Empyrean Heaven belongs to the Seraphim.</margin> First, Note that there are nine heavens. The **Empyrean heaven** is the court of the eternal King, that super-mundane house of the Mover of all; because of its order and infinite light, it corresponds perfectly to the order of the **Seraphim**, and from it all illuminations of souls proceed as if from a most fertile fountain.

### Book 10. The Ten-Stringed Lyre of Nature.

Second follows the starry heaven or firmament, into which the Great Craftsman <note>Referring to the Creator or Demiurge.</note> pours himself into the numerous instruments of things to be created; it corresponds beautifully to the <term>Cherubic order</term> <note>The Cherubim, the second highest order of angels, associated with divine wisdom and the "fullness of knowledge."</note> of intelligences. For the stars are nothing other than symbols of the notions within the human soul, from whose formal concepts is born the science proper to the Cherubim.

<margin>
What things are subject to the moving Intelligence of Saturn.
</margin>
<margin>
The Intelligence of Saturn, <term>Schabtai</term>, rules over Saturnine things.
</margin>
Third, the globe of Saturn (♄) correctly corresponds to the **Thrones** or to the intelligence <term>Schabtai</term> <note>Derived from the Hebrew *Shabbetai*, meaning Saturn; the author interprets it here as "my sitting" or "my rest."</note>. By its inflowing power, it generates in us a firm, fixed, and unshakable prudence; furthermore, it binds a person, as it were, fixed upon the throne of their own counsels. For this reason, it is called *Schabtai* by the Hebrews—that is, "my sitting"—and all things in the sublunary world that savor of a Saturnine nature, whether in stones, plants, or animals, are subject to it, as we have shown elsewhere.

<margin>
The Intelligence of Jupiter, **Zadkiel**.
</margin>
Fourth follows the globe of Jupiter (♃), which by its nature and properties corresponds beautifully to the choir of **Dominations**. For it is a beneficial planet, royal and full of majesty; hence it promises dominion and empire to those born under it, with its intelligence bestowing upright justice. Under its empire, all things of the sublunary world that savor of a Jovial <note>Jupiter-like</note> nature are subjected.

<margin>
The Intelligence of Mars, **Camiel**.
</margin>
Next follows the globe of Mars (♂), which, because of its fiery and scorching force, matches the **Virtues** best. By its power, while it burns the bile within us, it makes us fit to overcome arduous things with ease, and increases strength and fortitude. All things of the lower world endowed with a Martial nature are subject to this globe.

<margin>
The Intelligence of the Sun, **Schaphiel**.
</margin>
The globe of the Sun (☉), just as it holds the central body of the world, acts as the King and Prince of the whole, moderating all things by its power and authority. For this reason, it most appropriately corresponds to the middle order of **Powers**. Its intelligence produces life, prosperity, and glory within us; the bodies of a solar nature in the sublunary world harmonize perfectly with this, as has been said elsewhere.

<margin>
The Intelligence of Venus, **Hanael**.
</margin>
The globe of Venus (♀), a benevolent and most beautiful planet, matches the **Principalities**. Its intelligence, <term>Haniel</term> <note>Often associated with grace or the "Glory of God."</note>, instills in us the love of the most beautiful things and bestows the grace and benevolence of all people. Subject to this globe and the guardianship of its Intelligence are all things that correspond to it by a certain analogy of nature, which are called "Venereal," as was shown in the preceding sections.

<margin>
The Intelligence of Mercury, **Cochabiel**.
</margin>
The globe of Mercury (☿) is aptly joined with the **Archangels**. Just as the Archangels strive to conform all things to the image of the supreme Prince and to compose them so they may be joined to Him in perfect union, so also Mercury labors to bring vocal, formal, and rational numbers into a harmony with those same things—especially the composition of the rational number with the divine. Its Intelligence, <term>Cochabiel</term> <note>From the Hebrew *Kokab*, meaning "Star of God."</note>, teaches true concord and union with GOD, and endeavors to lead souls into GOD by that harmony, so that being perpetually joined to Him, they may break forth into perpetual hymns and praises of that eternal majesty. To this globe, all Mercurial things of the sublunary world are subject.

<margin>
The Intelligence of the Moon, **Levaniel**.
</margin>
Finally, the last globe of the celestial <term>Ennead</term> <note>A group of nine.</note> is the Moon (☽), which harmonizes best with the **Angels**, the last among the nine orders. Just as the Moon is closest to us, so are the Angels. Just as the Moon receives into itself the forces of all the higher planets to be communicated to the sublunary world, so also the Angels derive the illuminations received from higher minds down into us. Innumerable things could be said here concerning the influence of these peculiar virtues, but since we have reserved these for our *Hieroglyphic Theology*, we refer the reader there in due time.

Having thus seen the kinship and wonderful harmony of the first Ennead <note>The nine angelic orders.</note> with the second <note>The nine celestial spheres.</note>, let us now see how the Craftsman of all things produced all creatures of the sublunary world through a third Ennead, or a "squared three."

<margin>
How the Monad extended itself into the Dyad.
</margin>
The primeval <term>Monad</term> <note>The One, or God as the singular point of origin.</note>, the principle of all things, unfolding itself in time into the <term>Dyad</term> <note>The number two, representing duality or the split between spirit and matter.</note>, produced indefinite duality or matter. Since numbers flowed from the Monad and the Dyad, points from numbers, lines from points, surfaces from lines, and finally solid bodies from surfaces—namely, the four primary elements, the foundations of things. Since these were dealt with extensively in the first register, we do not wish to be more verbose here, but only to show in this place how the said four Elements, along with five grades of mixed beings, constitute the third Ennead, and how the elements...

# The Great Art of Consonance and Dissonance

...not only in nature, but also in the intellectual ennead <note>A group or set of nine, from the Greek *enneas*.</note>, and indeed in God Himself in His own way, so that the Musical concept of the world may be more clearly revealed through the Archetype <note>The original divine blueprint of the universe.</note>. The ennead comprises the four elements together with five grades of corporeal nature; these nine, joined together, constitute the following: Earth, Water, Air, Fire; stones or metals, plants, <term>zoophytes</term> <note>Organisms, like coral or sponges, historically thought to be intermediate between plants and animals.</note>, brute animals, and Man, of which the inferior world consists. Although these are physical, the most wise Creator and Harmonizer <note>original: *harmosta*</note> has linked them with such harmony to the other two worlds—the celestial and the angelic—that each exists in its own way within every world. Earth is the basis and foundation of the inferior world.

<margin>
In God, Angels, the heavens, and the earth in its own way.
</margin>
1. There is an "earth" in the Heavens, as we showed in the second Register; there is also an "earth" among the Angels, insofar as they are the firm seats of God and His footstool. In the Archetype of all things, there is a firm and most fertile nature, according to the scripture: "Let the earth be opened and bud forth a Savior" <note>original: "Aperiatur terra & germinet Saluatorem," a reference to Isaiah 45:8.</note>. Furthermore, there is elemental water: light, bright, cleansing, and washing all things.

<margin>
All things are in the heavens.
</margin>
2. There is also "water" in the heavens, which by its influence irrigates the earth—a mixing power such as that which the Moon <term>☽</term> and Jupiter <term>♃</term> pour into men. Among the Angels, it is a teaching and cleansing power, according to the verse: "Who coverest the upper rooms with waters" <note>original: "Qui tegis aquis superiora eius," from Psalm 104:3.</note>. In the Creator, however, it is the water of salvation, by which sins are washed away and man is regenerated, cleansed, and illuminated.

<margin>
Air is in all things.
</margin>
3. By elemental air we breathe, see, hear, and smell. There is also "air" in the heavens—that transparent nature that exposes the ornaments and riches of the world to our eyes. It exists also in the space of the Angelic world, where the harmony of blessed minds resonates as a vital breath and a thin aura. In the Creator, it is the highest and most perfect life and spirit, which He bestows by breathing into all things so that they may live and breathe.

<margin>
Fire is in all things.
</margin>
4. What elemental fire is to us, the Sun is in heaven; in the hierarchical world of angels, it is Seraphic ardor and fiery impulse, according to the verse: "Who makest thy angels spirits, and thy ministers a burning fire" <note>original: "Qui facis Angelos tuos spiritus, & ministros tuos ignem vrentem," from Psalm 104:4.</note>. Finally, in the Archetype, it is the ideal fire and spiritual light, by which all things are fathered, preserved, sustained, nourished, and increased. Therefore, the elements in God are certain nurseries and ideas of things to be produced—the first seeds and origins. In the Angels, they are distributed powers; in the heaven, they are analogous virtues; in the nature of things, they are seeds; and in the lower world, they are coarser forms.

And from this is born that admirable "concord of the world," by which the earth harmonizes with the Moon (the celestial earth); Water with Mercury <term>☿</term> and Venus <term>♀</term>; Air with Jupiter <term>♃</term> and Venus <term>♀</term>; and Fire with the Sun and Mars. Likewise, stones harmonize with Saturn <term>♄</term>; metals with Jupiter <term>♃</term>; <term>zoophytes</term> with Mars; insects with the Sun; birds with Venus; amphibians with Mercury <term>☿</term>; and quadrupeds with the Moon <term>☽</term>. All things harmonize with all others in a wonderful sympathy, both among themselves and with the rational soul. The soul's Ennead <note>Group of nine.</note> is collected from the 5 outer senses and the 4 inner senses—namely, common sense, imagination, appetite, and reason. These terminate at the Intellect as the tenth part. To this intellect, another purer Ennead of simple numbers—the nine orders of Angels—corresponds, so that within the soul there is a full image of the Angels and of God. This terminates in the tenth source: the supreme Father of all. The soul has a triple operation that is entirely consonant and harmonic: with this lower world in nature, with the heavens in the senses, and with the Angels in the intellect. It emerges into a "tetrad" <note>A group of four.</note> through the simple power of the soul; into an "ennead" through the 9 senses (5 corporeal and 4 incorporeal); and it reaches the "icosiheptad" <note>The number 27 (3 cubed).</note>, or 27—the idea of the total consummation of things—when, through understanding, it becomes all things.

## Corollary.

You see, therefore, how in our harmonic scheme, perfection is denoted by the unity of the whole world; variety and multitude of things contained within it are denoted by the number two; the analogous unity in the eternal triad, joining all things in fitting proportion, is denoted by the number three; the bond and link of the three worldly enneads explained just before is denoted by the number nine; and thus through the cube—which the Pythagoreans call "harmony"—the harmony of the whole is completed from the simple, the square, and the cubic number. Beyond this cube there is no further progress, since number by its own nature, once it has grown in length, breadth, and depth, cannot be further

### Book X. The Ten-Stringed Instrument of Nature

...cannot be extended. God, therefore, existing as one within Himself, is diffused into a multitude, just as unity is distributed into numbers, from which He never recedes in His own unique way. Indeed, from this unity, He gathers all the strings of the worldly <term>icosihebdadidis</term> <note>original: *icosihebdadidis*; a term derived from Greek meaning "twenty-seven." In this context, it refers to a cosmic scale of 27 steps or notes that Kircher uses to map the entire universe.</note> into one, rendering them elegant, tempered, and harmonious. Through this, the concord of like and unlike voices—that is, of genera, species, and individuals—is led back into unity. This happens while, according to a certain portion, He communicates to one thing 

<margin>
Divine Music.
</margin>
in a double proportion <note>An octave (2:1 ratio).</note>, to another in triple, to some in quadruple, to several in a <term>sesquialtera</term> <note>A ratio of 3:2, creating the interval of a perfect fifth.</note> or <term>sesquitertia</term> <note>A ratio of 4:3, creating the interval of a perfect fourth.</note>, and to others even in a <term>sesquioctava</term> <note>A 9:8 ratio, a whole tone.</note> or <term>sesquinona</term> <note>A 10:9 ratio, a minor whole tone.</note> proportion. From this, by necessity, various harmonic temperaments result from the constitution of the various octaves, double octaves, octaves-plus-fifths, fifths, fourths, tones, and other consonances. Yet the connection and intermingling of these is known only to Him who could truly say with the Preacher <note>original: *Ecclesiastico*; though the quote follows is from the Wisdom of Solomon 7:17-21.</note>:

> He himself gave me true knowledge of those things that are, so that I might know the disposition of the world, and the powers of the elements, and the completion and the middle of time, the changes of the successions, the endings of times, the mutations of customs, the dispositions of the stars, the natures of animals, the rages of wild beasts, the force of winds and the thoughts of men, the differences of shrubs, the virtues of roots, and finally all such things as are hidden and unforeseen I have learned.

These things are manifested either through the 

<margin>
How we are made omniscient.
</margin>
anointing of the Holy Spirit, or through the "Death of the Kiss" <note>original: *mors osculi*; a mystical term referring to a state of ecstatic union with the divine where the soul leaves the body.</note> as the more secret theologians speak, or according to the Platonists, by a certain essential contact of the ideas of the First Intellect itself, which is able to perform all things in the receiver. From this contact, as if from a union, images are conceived, the species of things are introduced, the soul is awakened, and it is purged with ambrosia and nectar from the contagion brought in from the Lethean stream <note>The river of forgetfulness in Greek mythology.</note>. You see that under this harmonic constitution of things, the divine mind—the <term>Archimusa</term> <note>The "Supreme Muse" or "Chief Musician."</note>—has tempered all things with musical numbers. And since all perfection in things consists in a perfect intermingling and temperament, there will be no secret in the nature of things so abstruse that one could not penetrate it by fitting the consonant to the dissonant in the <term>polychord</term> <note>A many-stringed instrument; here representing the complex system of the world.</note> of this worldly system, according to the rules handed down in the preceding pages.

<margin>
The greatest harmonic secret of all.
</margin>
I reveal the secret in very few words: Let the nine-stringed instrument <note>original: *Enneachordum*</note> of the soul be led back to the Hierarchical nine-stringed instrument, and that of the body to the celestial and starry one through <term>isophonon</term> <note>original: *ἰσοφωνον*; meaning "equal-sounding" or unison.</note>, and you will penetrate the secrets of secrets of which I have spoken—the most absolute knowledge of divine and human things, according to that saying of Saint John: *You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things.* This admirable music of that super-worldly Leader <note>original: *choragi*; the leader of a choir or ancient Greek dramatic chorus.</note> with the universe is shown in the preceding figure or diagram, in which you may find, as if in a synopsis, whatever has been said up to this point. I shall say nothing here of the internal peace 

<margin>
The incomprehensible sweetness and pleasantness of divine Music.
</margin>
and tranquility of the blessed minds and the dances of the souls; I shall say nothing of the incomprehensible symphony of Angels and men in that eternal Concert Hall of the Supreme Muse <note>original: *Archimusæi Odæo*</note>. Certainly, the sight and delight of all the most beautiful things of this world, compared to that, what else is it but vile straw, rotten chaff, and a tiny bit of the dregs of the earth? All imaginable harmony and music that the skill of human genius could ever invent, all conceivable pleasantness and sweetness of harmonic instruments, all excellence and perfection of human voices—what are they compared to that supreme music but the most dissonant growling of beasts, the howling of wolves, the grunting of pigs? What is all the harmonic pleasantness, sweetness, and softness of smells, tastes, and touch but stench, bitterness, and mere uncleanness? Just as eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man to conceive its most ordered and pre-eminent disposition, so the same can neither be explained by any concept of words, nor declared by any felicity and fecundity of the pen, nor penetrated by any deep scrutiny of the mind. There, not merely with three, four, or five, but with an ineffable symphony of most eminent voices, the entire Court of the Heavenly King and the super-worldly hall shall resonate through perpetual eternities, with the various classes of Saints arranged as if into certain choirs. There, the choir of Virgins, sounding among the choirs of Confessors, these among the Martyrs, and those among the choirs of Apostles and Patriarchs, all together according with the tripartite hierarchies of Angels, eternally resting at the fountain of the perennial water of life, they shall sing that eternal "Alleluia" with unfailing exultation to God as if to a supreme Leader of the Choir, who directs the symphony through His own wisdom.

# The Great Art of Consonance and Dissonance

with Him guiding, and the breath of His mouth animating the instrument, they shall play; where following the Lamb of God—who in this dwelling place of eternity is at once the one to be played upon, the instrument, and the music itself—they shall sing a new song; that wondrous wedding song and marriage hymn <note>original: *epithalamium & hymenæum*</note> of the Word of God betrothed to human nature in the womb of the immaculate Virgin; where the memory of labors and torments endured <note>original: *exanthlatorum*</note> in this world for the love of God, like a dissonant element mixed with the consonances of the eternal and most blessed life, shall coalesce through syncopation <note>A musical term where a rhythm is shifted; Kircher uses it here as a metaphor for how earthly suffering is "resolved" into heavenly joy.</note> into the sweetest and most perfect harmony of all. O unhappy lot of those who, becoming deafened by the deceptive and momentary goods of this calamitous life, by the noise of worldly ambition, and by the most dissonant cataracts of foul affections and pleasures, fall away from their hope of reaching that music we have described, which is to be perceived one day! O Great Harmonizer <term>Harmosta</term> <note>A Greek-derived term for a governor or regulator; here, Kircher uses it to describe God as the one who "tunes" the universe.</note> of all things, who disposes all things in number, weight, and measure; tune the nine-stringed instrument <term>enneachordon</term> <note>Referring to the nine choirs of angels in the celestial hierarchy: Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones, Dominions, Virtues, Powers, Principalities, Archangels, and Angels.</note> of my soul according to the good pleasure of Your divine will; stir all the strings of my soul to the praise and glory of Your name, so that I may love You with Seraphic ardor, seek You incessantly with the Cherubic scrutiny of the mind; let my soul be a throne where You may rest, where You may lie down at midday. Let the protection of the Dominions, Virtues, and Powers be present; place the Principalities over every untamed and rebellious crowd of my affections, so that I may serve You with Angelic purity forever. Let Your voice sound in my ears, for Your voice is sweet and Your face is beautiful; arrange in me 그 harmony of virtues, which You have disposed both in Yourself and in the supreme virtues from the beginning, so that proceeding from virtue to virtue—just as from tone to tone—I may reach the <term>diapason</term> <note>The interval of an octave; here used to mean the complete "octave" or full range of all virtues.</note> of all virtues and the fulfillment of all perfection. Thus fortified by this guard of virtues, I shall sing to You on the ten-stringed psaltery, and I shall praise and glorify You forever and ever. Amen.

## Epilogue of the entire work.

Thus far, therefore, the admirable works of the Best and Greatest Creator in the harmonic structure of the world have been discussed, as far as the powers of my intellect allowed. It remains now that, with eyes and hands removed from the table of demonstrations and lifted up to heaven, I may pray as a devoted suppliant to the Father of lights. O eternal Wisdom, the foundress and maker of things, who through the light of nature promotes in us the desire for the light of grace, so that through it You may transfer us into the light of Your glory: I give thanks to You, for You have delighted me in Your creation, and I have rejoiced in the works of Your hands. I give thanks because You have introduced me into the hidden concert hall <note>original: *odæum*</note> of Your divinity, where with even the slight whisper of Your infinite sweetness You have so Ravished my heart and so filled my ears that I was nearly deafened to all the delights and joys of earthly corruption, as if to the tumultuous cataracts of a falling world. Behold, I have now completed the work of my profession, using as much strength of intellect as You have given me. I have manifested the glory of Your works to the men who will read these labors of mine, as much as the narrowness of my mind could grasp of Your infinite magnitude. I have finished this sacred discourse, this hymn to God the Creator, judging this to be true piety: not that I should sacrifice hecatombs <note>An ancient Greek sacrifice of one hundred oxen.</note> of bulls to Him, or burn incense and cassia <note>An aromatic bark similar to cinnamon, used in biblical anointing oils.</note>, but first that I myself might learn, and afterwards teach others, how great He is in wisdom, how great in power, and of what sort in goodness. For I have always held it to be a proof of the most consummate goodness to wish to spread what is good and to envy it to no one. My mind has always been ready to philosophize as faultlessly as possible; if anything unworthy of Your counsels has been brought forth by me—a little worm born and nourished in the wallowing-place of sins—which You wish men to know, inspire me to amend it. I have not sought my own glory among men while proceeding in this work destined for Your glory; I earnestly pray that You forgive me for any such thing out of Your infinite mercy. Finally, may You deign to grant that this work of harmonic meditations may serve solely for Your glory and the salvation of souls.

->PRAISE BE TO GOD AND THE VIRGIN MOTHER.<-

->T H E  E N D.<-

Summary of the Imperial Privilege.

By the authority of Emperor FERDINAND III, it is cautioned that no one within the borders of the Holy Empire, and its hereditary Kingdoms and Dominions, shall print or sell, either in whole or in part, the Work entitled *Universal Music-making, or the Great Art of Consonance and Dissonance* <note>original: "Musurgia Universalis, sive Ars Magna Consoni & Dissoni"</note> by Father Athanasius Kircher of the Society of Jesus, for a period of ten years without the Author's permission; under the penalties contained in the Imperial letters. Given at Vienna, the 4th day of the Month of December, in the Year 1649.

Summary of the Catholic King’s Privilege.

By the authority of PHILIP IV, the Catholic King of the Spains, the same Decree is established for the same number of years throughout the Provinces of Belgium subject to Royal dominion, as is more broadly evident from his letters. Given at Brussels, July 10, 1649.

ADMONITION To Bookbinders.

The Illustrations <term>Iconismi: the engraved plates or diagrams.</term> marked (Vol. 2) belong to Volume 2 at the page number indicated there; the other Illustrations, however, in which the Volume is not assigned but only the page is noted, belong to Volume 1. The Frontispiece or Figure which contains the title of the Work with the name of the Author is to be placed before the Title of Volume 1. The Illustration of Apollo marked with Num. XI & XII should be placed before the Title of Volume 2. Finally, the Portrait of the Most Serene Archduke <note>Leopold Wilhelm of Austria, the work's patron.</note> should be placed before the Dedication in Volume 1.
